fields.description:
Discovered by the sibling sweep while fixing 12e4 (a stalled snapshot fetch burned the full 300s `_GIT_TIMEOUT`).

12e4 fixed the snapshot path: `_snapshot/git_fetch.fetch_origin` and `repo_snapshot._ensure_blobs_present` now pass `http.lowSpeedLimit`/`http.lowSpeedTime`, so a byte-starved transfer aborts on throughput in ~10s instead of at the wall-clock ceiling.

Three other NETWORK git calls still carry a 300s wall-clock bound and no low-speed abort, so each has the identical exposure:

- `src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py:367` (and the fetch at :401) — the review bot's own fetch of the Gerrit change, `_GIT_TIMEOUT = 300`. Closest sibling: same process, same per-review budget.
- `src/rebar/opcert_service/workspace.py:107,124` — `fetch --quiet review|tickets`, `_GIT_TIMEOUT = 300`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py:398,419` — `_FETCH_TIMEOUT = 300`.

Deliberately NOT in scope for 12e4: they are a different remote (self-hosted Gerrit) or a different command path, no stall has been measured on them, and folding them in would have widened an already-large change that was forced to split a module. The 30s callers (`_store/push.py`, `_store/sync.py`, `_store/event_append.py`, `_ref_lock.py`) are low value — 30s is already an order of magnitude tighter than the observed stall.

Reuse the seam 12e4 built: `rebar._snapshot.git_fetch.stall_abort_args()` and `is_stall_abort()` are module-public and take no snapshot-specific state, so each call site is a splice of `*stall_abort_args()` before the subcommand plus a decision about whether to retry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Each of the three 300s network fetch sites passes the low-speed options.
- [x] A test per site proves a zero-byte remote aborts as a stall, and that a dribbling remote is not aborted.
- [x] No new duplicate of the abort logic: the sites reuse `git_fetch.stall_abort_args()`.
